headline: 5 Ethereum-side contracts catalogued via Etherscan name-tag search; no official deployments doc, GitHub, or audits found; on-chain reads blocked by allowlist.
short_headline: 5 Ethereum contracts; no docs or audits

findings.text: Etherscan name-tag search returned 4 PulseChain-tagged contracts on Ethereum: Omnibridge Proxy (0x1715a3E4...aeba10d, $56M balance), Foreign AMB Proxy (0xd0764fae...d5636c), WETH Omnibridge Router (0x8ac4ae65...350f55), and pulsechaincom.eth ENS address (0x03cf40b9...cbc95e2). WPLS bridged token (0x97Ac4a24...755341) also surfaces from multiple community sources.

pulsechain.com website fetch returned only HTML metadata (no deployments page found). bridge.pulsechain.com exists per search results but could not be fetched. No canonical deployed-contracts documentation URL was discovered.
protocol.audit_links is empty; no audit PDFs found via website or search. Etherscan shows 'No Contract Security Audit Submitted' on the Omnibridge Proxy page.
protocol.github is not recorded. No official GitHub repository was discovered via website fetch or search results.

Protocol context specifies a single chain (Ethereum). PulseChain itself is a separate EVM chain; its Ethereum-side bridge contracts are the in-scope surface. Only Ethereum-side addresses are catalogued.
No factory contract identified in surfaced addresses. The Omnibridge and AMB proxies are individual bridge endpoints, not pool factories. No factory enumeration required.

Role taxonomy applied: Omnibridge Proxy = vault/router (holds bridged funds); Foreign AMB Proxy = other (message relay); WETH Omnibridge Router = router; owner address of WETH router = unknown actor class (address 0x610094aB... not further identified this run); WPLS = token; pulsechaincom.eth = other (ENS controller).

All five admin_addresses entries trace to Etherscan search result snippets appearing in this run's evidence. Truncated implementation address (0xA1077a29...) was not reconstructable to 40 hex chars and is recorded in unknowns instead.

rationale.verdict: Discovery run walked pulsechain.com (metadata only), Etherscan name-tag search (4 tagged contracts found), and community sources for bridged token addresses. Five Ethereum-side addresses are catalogued with evidence citations. No deployments doc, GitHub, or audits were found. On-chain DeFiPunkd API reads were not possible as constructed URLs were not in the allowlist (recorded in unknowns). Grade is unknown as this is a discovery slice.

Etherscan name-tag 'PulseChain: Omnibridge Proxy'; verified contract; balance $56,287,735.4 across 2 chains as of Aug-01-2026; 292,860 transactions; proxy pattern with implementation 0xA1077a29...a5D0f9a27; no audit submitted.
Etherscan name-tag 'PulseChain: Foreign AMB Proxy'; verified contract; 328,638 transactions; AMB (Arbitrary Message Bridge) relay contract for PulseChain bridge.

Etherscan page for pulsechaincom.eth ENS address; EOA/ENS controller associated with pulsechain.com domain.

Community list of PulseChain bridge token addresses; WPLS on Ethereum = 0x97Ac4a2439A47c07ad535bb1188c989dae755341; PLSX on Ethereum = 0x4AC429A7cdf2b533E2c0cFF1b017F2c344E864e2; HEX bridged to Ethereum = 0x46F6e9BbcCe8638b20EBBC83D33a2B5bfA9B7894.
L2BEAT entry for PulseChain bridge; describes it as a bridge to transfer assets from Ethereum to PulseChain; states 'Transfers are validated by set of trusted Validators'.

protocol_metadata.about: PulseChain is an Ethereum fork created by Richard Heart that launched as an independent proof-of-stake blockchain in May 2023, copying Ethereum's entire state at a snapshot block. Users bridge assets between Ethereum and PulseChain using the official bridge at bridge.pulsechain.com, which uses an AMB (Arbitrary Message Bridge) and Omnibridge architecture — locking tokens on Ethereum and minting wrapped equivalents on PulseChain. The Ethereum-side bridge infrastructure consists of a Foreign AMB Proxy for message relay and an Omnibridge Proxy holding bridged assets ($56M TVL as of August 2026), with transfers validated by a set of trusted validators rather than trustless cryptographic proofs.
